summary: At baseline 03d97b48a86d4b7d7bbedcb4441398ce3a9dadef, read the existing broad apt-subject privation definition and the target's exact conditional biconditional. The materialized Aristotle texts and live Aquinas De principiis naturae 1-2 supply positive support: generation concerns an eligible subject's missing form, and Aquinas explicitly identifies non-actuality as privation while distinguishing privation from arbitrary negation. The difference between visual faculty and present seeing is retained. Practical competence/acquisition evidence supports the capacity/act distinction defeasibly; no experiment or universal empirical proof is claimed. No substantive objection to Q in the selected identical subject/respect/context was identified; Boolean omission controls concern free predicates and are not real counterexamples. The proposed judgment favors the selected conceptual reading while keeping generic applicability and source-attribution boundaries explicit. Precise source URLs, passages, reuse results, assumptions and strengthening tests are persisted in docs/notes/potency-privation-support-investigation.md. No premise closure or source claim changed.
